sources.citation: Ramakrishnan A, Symeonidi A, Hanel P, Schmid KT, Richter ML, Schubert M, Colomé-Tatché M. epiAneufinder identifies copy number alterations from single-cell ATAC-seq data. Nat Commun 14, 5846 (2023).

claims.claim: Read counts per genomic region are used as a proxy for DNA copy number.
Bins with zero counts in more than 85% of cells are removed, intended to discard low-mappability regions; the threshold is adjustable.
Binned data are GC corrected with a LOESS fit of raw counts on GC content; the correction scales counts by mean count over the LOESS fit.
Profiles were reported concordant with scWGS from the same samples.

claims.claim: Bin filter nnz >= (1-0.85) n_cells; cell filter nnz > 0.35 n_bins; IQR outlier filters on totals and SD.
GC correction = mean/LOESS fit, np.rint + astype(int), raw saved, negatives clipped to 0, rows scaled to 1e5.
LOESS span 0.75; on exception returns the input counts.
Scale grid [0.5 median, min(1.2, 0.75 median)]; state weights (2, 1.5, 1/2..1/6); Holmes clip(k,1,3)-1; Watson <=1 / >=3.
Local and global permutation tests compare the observed statistic at the selected cut with fixed-length nulls (random_state 42).

sources.citation: Numbat-multiome: inferring copy number variations by combining RNA and chromatin accessibility information from single-cell data. Briefings in Bioinformatics 26(5): bbaf516 (2025).

claims.claim: Extends Numbat to scATAC alone and to paired RNA/ATAC; four modes: RNA-gene, RNA-bin, ATAC-bin, Combined-bin.
Median F1 > 0.9 across event types; benchmarks in multiple myeloma and CLL-to-Richter's syndrome validated against WGS.
Combining coverage and allelic signals improves detection of copy-neutral LOH.
Arm/focal event evaluation excluded segments below 10% of an arm or below 200 kb.

claims.claim: ATAC feature matrix = cell-by-bin integer counts of Tn5 fragments; reference = feature-by-cell-type normalized counts from normal samples.
Inputs prepared by inst/bin/pileup_and_phase.R (allele counts), get_binned_atac.R (fragments to bins), and a reference aggregated from normal samples.
Joint multiome assays (direct linkage in the same nucleus) not yet fully supported.

claims.claim: t(3;9)(p14;p21) is the cytogenetic event accompanying immortalization of MCF10A.
The 9p breakpoint is associated with a ~4 Mb deletion on der(9) including CDKN2A; the CDKN2A/B BAC is also deleted on the normal chromosome 9, making MCF10A null for p16/p15.
BAC arrays characterized gains/losses from rearrangements involving 1q, 5q and 8q (extents not visible in snippet).
